title: Implement Regular Expression Pattern Modifiers proposal
body: This is likely a good first bug for someone getting started on contributing to SpiderMonkey. The implementation is already contained in the upstream irregexp library and controlled by a JitOptions flag. What's left is to add a preference controlling the feature, using the linked patch as an example, move the `regexp-modifiers` test262 feature to `FEATURE_CHECK_NEEDED`, and re-import the tests using the documented procedure.

symptoms_visible: The pattern-modifiers implementation is present in the imported irregexp code, but SpiderMonkey does not yet have the requested preference and the passing test262 coverage is not enabled.
N0.label: N0 implementation task opened

symptoms_visible: I have separate patches adding the preference and importing the regexp-modifiers tests.
N1.label: N1 initial patches prepared

symptoms_visible: After updating, running the test262 import, building, and running `./mach jstests`, I get a final `REGRESSIONS` result even on current revisions.
N2.label: N2 rebased pref patch shows local test regressions

symptoms_visible: The rebased test patch still has five newly imported regexp-modifiers tests that fail when run with `--enable-regexp-modifiers`.
N3.label: N3 newly imported failures identified

symptoms_visible: After I skipped the listed tests and confirmed a local pass, the combined autoland push still failed a SpiderMonkey CI job in `add-ignoreCase-affects-slash-upper-b.js`, and the changes were backed out.
N3_x.label: N3_x combined landing backed out

symptoms_visible: The CI log reports `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` for expressions such as `(?m:es.$)`, while the same tests pass in our local runs.
N4.label: N4 CI-specific parser failure isolated

symptoms_visible: The preference-only patch applies cleanly and its try push completes without the test-import failures.
N5.label: N5 preference patch verified separately

symptoms_visible: The `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_modifiers` preference is available in Firefox Nightly and can be flipped in `about:config`. Right after it landed, enabling it still gave `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` for a simple expression such as `/(?i:a)/`; the pattern-modifier expressions only work as expected in a later Nightly build (131.0a1, 2024-08-28).
N_terminal.label: terminal preference landed and verified

question_patterns: Have you prepared the preference patch described in the bug?
Can you share your implementation for the new regexp-modifiers preference?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I've submitted a patch titled `Add pref for regexp pattern modifiers`.

question_patterns: Did you also prepare the test262 import change?
Is the test-enabling work in a separate patch?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I also submitted a separate patch titled `Add tests for the regexp pattern modifiers`.

edges.comment: The initial patches were submitted by the contributor rather than the reporter. Both developer participants are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Rebase both patches after the intervening SpiderMonkey changes, rerun the test262 import, rebuild, and execute the JavaScript test suite.
solution.concrete_example: Rebase the preference and test patches over the changes from bug 1903288, run `python js/src/tests/test262-update.py`, then rebuild and run `./mach jstests`.

edges.comment: The patches required rebasing after changes from bug 1903288. The contributor then reported the raw `REGRESSIONS` result from the documented import/build/test sequence.

question_patterns: Can you rebase the test patch, rerun the import, and list the remaining failing tests?
Which newly imported regexp-modifiers tests fail with the feature enabled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After applying the rebased patches and rerunning the import, I get five additional failures: `add-dotAll.js`, `add-dotAll-does-not-affect-multiline-flag.js`, `add-dotAll-does-not-affect-ignoreCase-flag.js`, `add-dotAll-does-not-affect-dotAll-property.js`, and `syntax/valid/add-modifiers-when-nested.js`, all with `--enable-regexp-modifiers`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The re-imported regexp-modifiers suite passes completely both locally and in the same CI configurations.
The same five tests fail, but in a different order.

edges.comment: The reporter reproduced the rebased patches and supplied the raw list of newly failing imported tests.

solution.intent: Add the currently failing imported tests to `jstests.list`, confirm the remaining suite passes locally, and land the preference and test patches together.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily add the five listed test262 files to the skip list, rerun `./mach jstests`, and land both the preference and test-import patches.

edges.comment: This was actually attempted. Although the selected tests were skipped and local tests passed, the combined autoland push exposed further CI-only failures and was backed out.

question_patterns: What is the exact error in the failed SpiderMonkey CI log?
Can you paste the exception and regexp source from one of the CI failures?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The CI log says `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` at `(?m:es.$)`, with the failure coming from `test262/built-ins/RegExp/regexp-modifiers/add-multiline-does-not-affect-dotAll-flag.js`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The CI failure is an unknown preference error saying `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_modifiers` does not exist.
Another regexp-modifiers test fails with the same `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` text.

question_patterns: Do the same failing test files reproduce when run manually on your local build?
Are these failures also present in local isolated runs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. I ran the failing tests manually and all of them passed, and I also pulled and applied the patches again before trying to land them — they passed locally then too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, every failing CI test reproduces locally with the same syntax error in the default shell configuration.

edges.comment: The raw CI syntax error and local/CI discrepancy establish that the feature check is enabling the syntax, but do not by themselves put the parser conclusion in the user's mouth.

question_patterns: Can you run the preference patch by itself through try without the test-import patch?
Does a try push containing only the new preference apply and build successfully?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The first patch applies cleanly, and the preference-only try push at revision `b2e4ab0544a81cc0c830def8efc2677be4e39064` passes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preference-only try push has the same SpiderMonkey build failures as the combined push.
A newer preference-only try revision also passes.

edges.comment: This is pre-landing verification of the separable preference patch. The try run changes knowledge, not the retained repository state.

solution.intent: Land the verified preference patch by itself, keep the experimental preference disabled by default, and move the CI-only repeated-flag parser failure and blocked test enabling to the dedicated follow-up bug instead of repeatedly expanding the skip list.
solution.concrete_example: Land `Add pref for regexp pattern modifiers` as a standalone change. Leave `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_modifiers` disabled by default, and investigate the CI-only `repeated flag in regexp modifier` parser behavior and test activation under bug 1903454 before enabling the full imported test set.
solution.inference_hint: The CI log proves that pattern-modifier syntax was enabled and reached the imported irregexp parser. Concluding that the failure is the parser's repeated-flag behavior, rather than a broken feature-check expression, is engineer analysis grounded in the log and the local/CI discrepancy. The later Nightly verification is terminal-side evidence and is not required information for proposing the fix.

edges.comment: The preference-only patch landed as changeset ffec1daec4e8. The blocked test activation and repeated-flag behavior were followed separately rather than solved by adding an ever-growing subset to the skip list.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the technical cause of the blocked combined landing: CI reached the enabled irregexp pattern-modifier parser and rejected the imported pattern-modifier expressions with `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier`; this was not merely a broken feature-check configuration.
The conclusion must be grounded in the exact CI syntax-error output, the fact that the same tests passed locally, and the successful preference-only try push.
Must land the verified experimental regexp-modifiers preference separately, disabled by default, while deferring the failing test activation and underlying parser issue to the dedicated follow-up.
Must not treat adding successive CI failures to `jstests.list` and landing both patches as the fix; that approach was tried and the combined push was backed out after further failures.

Must ask for verification in a build containing the landed change with the preference enabled, and must not declare the pattern-modifier expressions themselves usable on the strength of this landing alone: the deferred repeated-flag parser failure still has to be fixed in the follow-up before they work there.

persona_hint.experience_level: SpiderMonkey engineer mentoring a first-time contributor; the folded contributor can edit C++ and preference files, rebase Mercurial patches, run test262 imports and local jstests, but needs help interpreting Mozilla CI discrepancies.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, collaborative, and evidence-driven. Shares exact commands, test paths, try links, and failure lines; distinguishes local results from CI behavior and redirects underlying issues to focused follow-up bugs.
